display_title: 雾方福地 - Into the Emberlands

reviews.text: its fun cuddly cute and unforgiving when you died if you die your inventory is lost and all upgrades make you reset to the beginiing of your run the town lvl stays the same so you will have the same progress its just all upgrades are lost give it a try its fun to play and cozy i cried when i died cuz i lost all my good stuff :( i rate it 10/10

《雾方福地 - Into the Emberlands》是一款色彩鲜艳、节奏舒缓的休闲探索+村庄建造游戏；玩家将扮演携光者，在这被瘴气所笼罩的黑暗世界中，依靠提灯有限的余烬驱散迷雾，进行外出探索，不断收集资源、解救迷失的村民，并重建失落的村庄。 [h1] 反复探索重建村庄[/h1] 由于外出的每一步都会消耗提灯中的余烬、耗尽便迎来迷失失败，因此玩家需要确保剩下的余烬足以回到村庄、适可而止的进行探索收集。 通过反复的探索收集、玩家可以将从收集的资源与解救的村民投入到村庄重建升级，从而解锁新的功能建筑、购买补给品，获取更进一步探索的能力；包括和迷雾中的生物进行交易，升级提灯容量、背包栏位、金钱上限，通过斧头稿子收集资源的同时减少障碍、让道路变得更加畅通，都能让玩家下一次的外出走得更远。 [h1] 益智又轻松的探索[/h1] 其实这种有限余烬下反复来回、升级设备走的更远的游戏过程，在“漫漫长夜”等生存模拟游戏中到是很常见，相同点就在于有一个数值限制，例如抗寒游戏中的温度、饥荒游戏中的饱腹度、潜水游戏中的氧气瓶。但相比于这些需要考验效率与熟练度的实时模式，《雾方福地》按照走格子计算的模式则只需要玩家稍微留神保留余烬、不贪就都能安全回归。 包括回到村庄后、村里的篝火就会将提灯中的余烬重新补满，因此除了斧头稿子有耐久，其余没啥需要考虑的资源消耗问题，属于是益智又轻松的休闲探索。就是不知道后续内容与更新会不会有机制上的变动、为游戏增添难度，比如升级村庄到一定进度后，就需要烧木头来维持村里的篝火啥的。 [h1]总结[/h1] 《雾方福地》是一款画风可爱、色彩鲜艳、节奏舒缓的休闲探索+村庄建造游戏，吞噬一切的瘴气将世界笼罩在黑暗之中，唯有依靠提灯中有限的余烬才不会迷失；玩家将扮演携光者，收集资源重建失落的村庄、解救迷失的村民。 由于外出的每一步都会消耗提灯中的余烬，需要适可而止的进行探索；利用收集到的资源建设新的设施、与迷雾中的生物进行交易，升级提灯容量、拆除道路阻碍，每次出行都能让玩家下一次走得更远。总的来说，休闲益智、趣味性还行。 [quote]加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/GHYX]干货游戏[/url]&关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35106417/]咱的鉴赏家[/url]，不定期为大家带来游戏体验分享，也期待您来一起分享自己的游戏体验干货~[/quote]

If you are looking for a good cozy summer game, step into the enchanting world of Into the Emberlands. Exploration game is rogue-twist that is about rebuilding your village while threatened by a mysterious glooming miasma. Embark on a cozy journey a world full of small and big adventures.

[h1]《雾方福地》：闲暇时的惬意之选[/h1] 《雾方福地》是由Tiny Roar开发、Daedalic Entertainment发行的一款融合地图探险和基地建设的小清新风冒险游戏，发售三天，在Steam上虽然评价人数不多、但却获得了100%好评——这是什么概念？它意味着所有购买这款游戏的玩家里头没有一个人对其感到不满。尽管游戏玩法简单，却能在压力繁重的当下为玩家提供一个心灵的港湾。 相信有不少小伙伴跟俺一样是被游戏清新可爱的画风所吸引，作品采用了low-poly风格，我们的主角是一个可爱的粘土人，从森林的一个角落开始了自己的冒险。虽然模型相比较封面来说在游戏里失去了一丁点魅力，不过蹒跚的步伐、笨拙的身姿看着就非常让人喜爱，而伴随着空灵的音乐，也消去了许多烦闷的心情，让你在游戏里无时无刻不感到惬意。 玩法方面，《雾方福地》同样没有进行太复杂的设计——毕竟它的定位就是「治愈向作品」，过于复杂的玩法只会让人血压上涌。我们从一个小地块开始，绕着光亮探索森林，采集资源、与村庄NPC互动完成任务，不断建设我们的基地，最后在森林中打造一个属于自己的王国。从一个小小地方寸之地开始，到一片梦幻般的通化基地结束，这是一段独属于你自己的有趣冒险。 但同时作品又不仅仅是为了休闲，制作组还是为玩家在探险时设置了一点数值限制，以便让你更加感受到「游戏」的存在感而并非只是将其当做一个步行模拟器，虽然在游戏里的数值管理仍旧非常简单，基本上没有太多的生存压力。 当然，游戏的节奏也相当慢，尤其体现在走路上，如果你是个急性子或许会有点捉急。但必须要搞明白的一点在于，它本身是个休闲向的作品，玩它就是让你放松的，所以这种「慢节奏生活」也是制作组的有意为之，目的就是调剂玩家的心情、在忙碌的工作之后拥有一段休闲惬意的时光。 [code]双语评测，认准我们： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]双语评测[/url] Make Chinese and English speaker feel at home： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]Bilingual Curator[/url][/code]
蚂蚁搬山，体验……说实话很平凡。 回合制计步数，从外边砍树捡石头带回村庄，升级建筑过主线，主线看成就大概要升级十几次村庄吧，可能最多10小时？走太多步不回家就会憋死，然后你的背包、步数上限和钱上限就会初始化，所以尽量别死。 30块吃不到答辩，但喝了一杯白开水。 嗯，心痛的感觉。

[h1]少年，你相信光么？[/h1] 在《雾方福地》这个可爱的卡通童话世界里，幸福已经不再，因为可怕的瘴气已经笼罩整个世界，碰到瘴气的人都会迷失，如今整个世界自由我们这个小村庄里还拥有能驱散瘴气的“余烬”，我们需要做的就是利用这最后的“余烬”光芒壮大村庄，寻回所有迷失的纳克，解开瘴气的秘密，拯救整个世界。 游戏里我们需要操纵新一代的携光者手提“余烬提灯”进入被瘴气笼罩的森林进行探索，想要扩大村庄，第一步当然是为村庄增加人口，因此出发后记得盯着右上角的指南针上的小点点（这是《七龙珠》里的龙珠感应器？），向着小点的方向走必然能寻到那些迷失的同伴，之后还得在“余烬提灯”里的余烬耗尽之前一起回到村庄才算安全。“余烬提灯”只要进入村庄范围，就会通过中央的“余烬塔”（就是那个大红蜡烛）补充满所有“余烬”。 不得不说，这群叫做纳克的家伙真是太懒了，我们作为携光者经过重重危险，好不容易把他们这些迷失在瘴气之内的家伙带回村里，他们竟然还要我们弄个房子或者商店给他们住！！！他们这是忘记了自己在瘴气里风餐露宿提心吊胆迷失自我的日子了么！真是可恶！ 除了增加人口之外，当然就是资源了！每次出发我们还需要带上斧头和稿子，这样遇到一些被困住的纳克还能顺手救回来，再不济也能用来收集挡路的资源（这当然只是玩笑），斧头和稿子是我们冒险过程中除“余烬提灯”外最为重要的道具，每次升级完村庄后记得优先升级长老处！这样才能获得更高级的！ 探索森林的过程中，有时还能遇到各种巨魔和长脖子母鸡等奇妙生物，和他们互动能获得各种好处和帮助，运气好些甚至还能提高“提灯”和背包容量，相当关键！有时候还会遇到各种“诱惑巨手”，能用“余烬”与其交易获得好处，但是“诱惑”俩个字始终不是说着玩的，一个把持不住，计算“余烬”错误，可能就会倒在踏入村庄的最后一步上，永远的成为“迷失者”的一员，游戏也就只能进入下一个轮回了！ 整体而言，《雾方福地》的玩法还是相当不错的，轻微的肉鸽元素让我们每次开场能会随机生成不同的地图地形环境，让每场冒险都能有全新的体验，就这么提着提灯、计算步数、规划路径、扩建村落、驱散瘴气，成为一个相信光的少年来拯救这个世界吧！ [quote] 游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯，(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧ [url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见 [/quote]

For science, I let my ember burn out to see what happens. Losing inventory items is absolutely understandable, but you'll also lose all of your character progression and essentially start from scratch and have to farm all over again. If you have an upgraded town, you won't have those natural upgrades from town quests to easily allow further exploration. Just a little explorer beware.

I have now played Into the Emberlands for almost 20 hours. After about 8 or 9 hours I reached the maximum level of the Embertower and completed the game. Nevertheless, the game has continued to hook me. I kept trying to unlock all the achievements for the game. AFTER I WAS LOOKING FOR THIS ONE NPC FOR 10 HOURS AND WAS ALMOST DESPERATE AND NEARLY CRIED, I actually found him and was able to complete the game 100%. I have found my peace and can finally finish the game... until there are content updates and I can cry again. 10/10 gud game. can recommend.

画风挺可爱的，没发售的时候看到推荐就加入心愿单了。 这几天刚好看到在打折，就买来玩了。 本来前几天太肝了，蛮喜欢蛮适合这个很慢节奏的游戏，全流程下来10小时内能通关... 下面是我很不开心的原因： 1、至于我为什么玩了16小时，就是因为有一个成就要使用前哨站，我地图跑的我自己都想哭了，就真的没见过在哪儿有那么一个建筑...而且成就提示首次使用前哨站，那应该能用几次吧，像是路边的金钥匙，厨师，郊外的献祭花坛，还有个酋长还是啥的都是感觉比较少的吧，至少也找到过几次，就这个前哨站，16小时一个都没看到... 很难受... 2、而且中文翻译有问题，左上角提示需要的村名和材料数量永远都对，你还要自己一个个跑再去看一眼，但凡记性差点，真的难受... 3、作为一个收集物资升级的游戏，每一次升级除了身上的东西地上的东西会消失，作为一个屯屯鼠玩家真的很难受...辛辛苦苦跑那么远，收集很多东西，还要取舍那些不要了，就不能设计一个仓库？或者箱子么，每次死在外面东西也都会消失，家里也没有，升级的灯也会掉，连死两次真的难受无比。 4、作者应该根本没有考虑有玩家会长久玩的打算，就像我面具那些没了，通关游戏了，就不会再给你刷新了，就很难受，我还想再找那个前哨站，如果你建筑升到满级就再也不会刷装备出来了... 5、然后就是背包，真的太少太少太少了，你总得带点斧头稿子吧，还要剪刀把，石头不用就算了，木头可以换燃料吧，然后还有三种花，还有水晶，还有三种试剂，还有那个一沓纸一样的，还有蓝图，那么多东西，就8个格子？？？？ 6、说到背包，更难受的是没有满级提示，还是可以花水晶升级，其实已经满级了结果花了7个水晶去升级，诸如此类，包括村子里的鸡哥送的东西也是，满级了还是没得换其他的，选来选去都是已经升级过的东西，就相当于什么都没给，浪费了机会。是不是作者自己很喜欢数字8，水晶背包上限8个，背包上限8个，灯笼上限180，我就说怎么都买不到整数，升级了两次才发现全打水漂了...满级了你哪怕给我们还点钱都好啊，真的好亏... （还有没有什么攻略和指引，玩的时候也不知道，工具不能丢在地上，特别占格子，直到最后查成就查steam讨论看到作者置顶说吧工具悬停在灯笼上，可以销毁工具，但是这点游戏里面并没有说明，所以导致我要腾格子还要找个地方吧斧头稿子用完，要不就一直在身上，真的很难受） 7、手柄操作很难受，鼠标操作也是逆天，没有放大缩小，滚轮是左右旋转，还有个提示是什么放大的按键，提示的是（TutorialCameraPan）你来告诉我这是什么按键，让我看的更远？ 综上所述，如果你能接受就买来玩吧，而且不太适合急性子人，因为走路真的很慢很慢很慢，跑图也罢了，在家找个需要升级的NPC或者建筑真的要急死人... 祝你们玩得愉快吧，我挺不愉快的.

I fell in love with this game as soon as i saw the trailer, (my partner bought me this because i said it looked like something i would love to play and he surprised me). It is the BEST GAME I HAVE EVER PLAYED. ABSOLUTELY AMAZING! Such a nice, relaxing, chilled game. You roam around in the dark looking for objects to complete your little tasks, some of the levels can take an hour but the time just flies past. The only thing i would point out is it is in early access and the water is glitchy but doesn't affect game play at all. But overall EVERYONE SHOULD BUY THIS IT IS SO WORTH THE MONEY. I can not wait for more levels.
怎么说呢，画风确实很可爱，但游戏表现比较平庸，奖励也没有成就感，总之就是来来回回折返，人物又不能加速移动，很需要耐心，而且引导有些不足，比如我升级一个建筑需要8费金币，但我上限5费不知道怎么办，直接卡住我了，望正式版得到调整。喜欢这种风格的小伙伴可以参考一下。
A short sweet, fantasy-apocalyptic Rougelike.

[h2]游戏介绍[/h2] 《雾方福地 - Into the Emberlands》是由Tiny Roar工作室研制，Daedalic Entertainment宣发的一款超可爱手绘画风的休闲冒险策略类角色扮演游戏。余烬之地曾经是一片美丽富饶的土地，这里文化繁荣，可是有一天一股神秘的瘴气将整个世界笼罩在黑暗之下，被触碰到的事物都会被遗物，只剩下我们一个小村庄，因此我们要找到瘴气的源头，拯救世界！ 游戏的画风特别特别可爱，从人物、场景甚至是主界面和彩蛋都是涂鸦手绘风，包括我们小人走路的姿势都特别的Q萌，游戏中还加入了许多幽默有趣的梗，例如最开始村庄里的守卫“直到我的膝盖假装中了一箭”。 [h2]拓展地图维修基地[/h2] 我们扮演的提灯者因为携带者余烬提灯，因此可以驱散掉周围的瘴气并且提供视野。游戏中我们一开始的村庄破败不堪，只有几个坚守幸存下来的村民指引我们，我们需要带着我们的提灯，在大地图上自由的探索收集散落的材料。可以通过收集到的材料维修基地里损坏的建筑物，解锁新的功能。在大地图中探索时还会遇到各种迷失之人，我们需要不断的将迷失之人带回我们的村庄，帮助我们维修建筑（实际上是维修建筑的材料里有迷失之人2333） 我们每次移动都会消耗一格提灯余烬，初始共有30格余烬能量，我们可以通过完成完成野外NPC的任务获得余烬水晶、金币或者其他资源奖励，再带着余烬水晶去寻找余烬母鸡兑换余烬提灯的能量上限和其他材料。但是倘若我们不幸消耗完所有的提灯但是还没回到营地补充，则会直接结束游戏，也成为一名迷失之人，但是基地的建设进度会保留下来，地图和身上的物品以及提灯上限都会重置。 [h2]在大地图中自由探索[/h2] 地图上会随机生成许多木材、岩石，运气好还能遇到各种各样的例如斧子、稿子等现成工具用于摧毁在地图上的资源并且获得资源，而且玩家处于一片森林之中，在探索的时候经常会被树木或者矿石挡住最短的路线需要绕路，这时就可以用工具摧毁资源开拓出一条最近的道路节省提灯消耗。 探险中我们还会随机遇到许多功能各异的建筑和NPC，地图上会有随机散落的余烬，可以提供5点余烬能量和随机的资源；会有专业的厨师长鸡，可以用收集到的美食与他交换资源或者水晶；懒惰的巨魔会为我们提供各种资源收集的任务，给予我们金钱或者水晶奖励，还有许多有趣的功能等着玩家探索，我们可以甚至可以收集材料维修地铁站，在不同的站点之间穿梭。 [h2]总结[/h2] 总的来说，本作的画风是最大的亮点，而游戏的玩法非常休闲惬意，配上可爱卡通的画面和轻度策略的走格子玩法，非常适合闲暇时候消磨时光，推荐~ [quote]关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/42276832//]鸿源鉴游组」 [/url] [/quote] [u][b] 会当逢佳游，始可见鸿源。 [/b][/u]

[h1]简评：迷雾幸存者 [/h1] 本作是一款手绘美术风格的模拟经营游戏。游戏的核心机制为余烬机制（光源），玩家离开村庄每走一步会消耗提灯中的余烬，玩家需要在光源消耗完毕之前完成一次探索，带回幸存者和各种物资。在探索过程中，可以遇到各种随机余烬、物资以及可以进行资源交易的NPC，玩家需要把控好提灯中余烬的量避免无法返回。游戏的流程较为线性，玩家以升级余烬塔为核心目标，外出探索获得材料后升级建筑，进而满足升级余烬塔的条件。 [h1]评价：探索-收集-升级，标准模拟经营框架[/h1] 本作的核心循环相当简单，基本所有的物资产出都在非安全区（迷雾区域），因此玩家需要不断往返于安全区（村庄）和非安全区，进行资源的搬运。收集到资源后就可以升级村庄中的各种建筑，，升级完所有建筑后就可以升级余烬塔，解锁下一个阶段，再进行探索收集-升级建筑-升级余烬塔的下一个循环。 游戏的核心机制便是余烬机制（光源），玩家离开村庄每走一步会消耗提灯中的余烬。这与沙盒游戏中常见的生存机制类似，都是旨在通过加入限制进而对玩家的资源管理提出要求。说实话对于沙盒游戏来说，这么做是为了平衡探索与建造之间的体验比重，让玩家不会一味的探索or建造。但对于本作来说稍显多余，因为村庄建造是点一下就完事儿的东西。它更像是题材的一种包装，但代价就是走不了多远就被迫回家。 本作的探索要素不多，除开各种资源（散落在地上的斧头、木头石块和幸存者）之外，最常见的是余烬团，包含少量余烬和少量物资，玩家拾取到之后可以延长探索的时间。其次是各种NPC，比如提交木头给你晶石的巨魔、提交晶石给你背包or钱袋升级的母鸡、诱惑之手等等。不过看上去地图似乎是随机化生成的，大量的美术资源复用使得道路没有辨识度，一旦走远就必须依靠指南针才能找到回家的方向。 整体而言是一款比较中规中矩也比较常规没有玩法创新的模拟经营游戏，产品的差异化设计选在了绘本风美术上。看得出来制作组在美术上还是投入了不少心血的，3D小人的建模完成度很高，各种UI基本也是美术风格高度统一。 [h1][quote=] [table] [tr] [th] 欢迎关注 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/7421824]双鱼星✪ω✪皇家飛机场[/url][/th] [/tr] [tr] [th] 也欢迎━(*｀∀´*)ノ亻!各路大佬大佬加群啦，群号在组页面 [/th] [/tr] [/table] [/quote][/h1]

[i]Into the Emberlands[/i] is a cozy exploration game built around a roguelite core mechanic. As the Lightbearer, you are tasked to venture out into the wilds to collect various resources. These will be used to rebuild your town - the last remaining settlement in a world devoured by an unknown darkness called Miasma. The look and feel and the gameplay to some extent are very similar to a classic time management game (think of “12 Labours Of Hercules” games), but [i]Into the Emberlands[/i] is NOT exactly a time management game. Instead of the player’s actions depending on the recharge time of the production buildings, the Lightbearer carries a lantern that loses its charge with every step that he takes outside of the town area but fills up as soon as he steps back into town. Thus, how far out you can travel strictly depends on the amount of light stored in your lantern and while there are several ways to partially replenish it on your way, your expeditions will always be gated by your lantern’s capacity. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3447180298 When exploring the wilds, you get to collect resources, save fellow lost Lightbearers and exchange resources or special items that you find on the way for other resources, upgrades or more substantial rewards. There are several biomes to traverse, but they’re located radially on the map (with the town being at the center), thus reaching them can be done only after you expand your lantern capacity accordingly. The pace at which you progress and how far out you can travel with each run is quite satisfying. The game doesn’t feel grindy at all, and the runs always have a comfortable length - usually, your lantern capacity (including the amounts you can replenish on the way) is big enough to explore the world in one direction until you meet the next biome. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3447180138 Unlike time management games in which the order of your actions matters for optimizing your pathing, exploring the world in an optimal way is not of utmost importance here. What matters instead is that with any new tile you visit you have enough energy left to return to town, otherwise you die. Dying can substantially set you back, even if the already completed objectives for that stage will not be reverted. You lose the items in your inventory and the resources acquired during that expedition, and perhaps what hurts the progression the most is losing all the upgrades you purchased during that run (lantern capacity, inventory size and the amount of coins you can hold). The amounts you lose still feel rather harsh, despite the developers changing this system to be much less punishing than on release. Luckily, I had only one death but even if it was rather early in my gameplay, it did set me back by around two hours. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3447180186 The game suffers from the absence of a storage space, clearly noticeable mid and late-game. As you encounter new biomes, you will start amassing new types of resources. Considering that your inventory is very limited (max. 8 slots when fully upgraded) and that it has to hold not only basic resources but also processed ones (flasks), as well as tools to gather these and other rare spawns, it’s easy to see that it gets filled very quickly. As a workaround for the tight space, the game allows you to drop resources to any tile and pick them up later, but whenever you upgrade your town these will be lost because the map is fully regenerated. The lack of a storage mechanic and the cumbersome management of the inventory slots have been the community's top complaints. Yet it's been almost a year and the devs decided to focus on implementing other mechanics rather than addressing the most critical one. It took me around 14 hours to finish the game, including obtaining all the achievements (none of them are missable). [i]Into the Emberlands[/i] was a very colorful, fun and relaxing experience and the roguelite mechanic makes the game heavily replayable, however, it does have its flaws and my gameplay was far from bug-free. It's kind of neither here nor there Here's the deal: early-game here requires somewhat intense resource management as you can barely make it a few screens away from the village before running out of ember and perishing. Then you gradually upgrade your lantern to the point where your primary enemy will be your greed. So if you're here for a cozy time, you'll hate the early-game and perhaps like the mid/late-game, and if you like a challenge, you'll love the early game and might not like watching your character leisurely walk over a hundred-something tiles before you find something interesting (and possibly have to walk back for a recharge if you can't find a teleporter nearby). There are also other little inconveniences - e.g. anything you couldn't fit in your inventory will be lost whenever you advance the village to the next level, so you can't stockpile quest materials or harder-to-get biome-specific ones; there's a limit for how much you can upgrade one or other stat, but you'll keep getting quests that reward now-useless upgrades that you'll still have to complete to advance the village. Personally I ran out of patience. A bit of a shame, really

A deeply terrible game. To call it "cozy" is like calling Super Meat Boy "casual" - aside from the cute graphics, it is extremely tense! You need to constantly manage your resources, particularly because failures are punished with unclear setbacks, which cost dearly! At one point my setup was reduced to half, while I was sure that I was somewhat safe in the reset. Speaking of reset - you can force a reset (i.e. death), and you may need to do so, because the fast travel system can put you in a spot, from which you just cannot exit anymore. Meaning, in my case, that one gets set back a painful amount through no fault of one's own. Similarly, you can drop some of your stuff on purpose (but annoyingly not every item), and you can put it where you cannot pick it up again. Everything in the game is very randomized, and this also applies to the fast travel points. You may be on the hunt for one travel points forever, but then again, you may get three on the same screen! The same applies to virtually everything you may want to find - you may encounter a wasteland without that one thing in sight, or a whole bunch of them in one cluster. This is particularly problematic in the beginning, where resources are scarce(r), and one struggles to move ahead. Your second main enemy is the tiny inventory. Or to be more precise, the tiny inventories, because you have three distinct bags for different resources. The main one is already annoying as hell, because tools that provide resources have tiny stacks (e.g. an axe in the beginning has two uses, and even the top tier axe has eight), and the resources need to be crammed into the same space as the tools themselves. Yes, the resources stack well, but managing a collection of, say, 40 of something becomes a real nuisance. The other two inventories are for currency-like items, and you will find (especially in the beginning) that you either have zero of those items, or receive a bunch of them at the same time, making the crucial resources go to waste. At the same time, you cannot waste items from the main inventory directly, so you often need to throw something out, pick a different item collection up, throw the item you wanted to waste away, and then pick up the original item again. Fun. Finally, there is the upgrade/crafting system, which is poorly explained, and buggy. For example, you will get a lot of rewards that seem to indicate that your inventory or light capacity will go up, but they won't, because they are capped (light at 220, coins at 60). Some crafting stations need upgrades first, before you can craft the thing, you actually wanted, others may have upgrades, but those may be optional in the sense that you can still proceed without the upgrade. Unfortunately, there is no way to look up, what is crafted how, and where - there is no in-game option, and no wiki. Had my original experience with the game been a bit better, I would have started a wiki myself, but I ended up with just being happy that this ordeal was over.

8/10 This game is enjoyable once you understand its rules. It has simple mechanics with a limited number of movement points, and while exploring you come across different ways to extend your journey and gather the resources you need. The main thing is not to get greedy and to know your limits. The beginning can be rough: tools are limited, the number of moves is small, and the paths are tough. The game feels like a puzzle, where you try to figure out the most efficient way to collect resources and make it back. By the middle of the game, resources become commonplace — gold can be obtained from almost everything, gold can buy anything you need, and outside the base there are many easy ways to replenish your moves. The game completely shifts from a “puzzle” stage into an “exploration” stage. Once you know a few key rules, you can always return to base safely: - You should always have as many moves left as you spent getting away from the base. - Or build your route through furnaces and other sources of moves, while also keeping track of how many moves you have as resources in your inventory. - Items you do not need right now can be dropped on the ground, including at the base. They will disappear if you upgrade the tower, because the map refreshes. Pros: - Graphics and art style - Unique movement and exploration mechanics. - Procedural terrain generation with a sufficient number of objects. - Variety of zones. - Object RNG: makes it interesting to search for what you need instead of just going in and out. It gives a real explorer vibe. Cons: - Slow character movement speed, especially once travel distances get longer. - Sometimes quests do not show the required resource amounts. - Repeating quests across several stages. - Object RNG: there is no stability or even a guarantee that a zone of a certain size will contain the object you need. It can take a lot of time to find it. - Sometimes tiles invincible, just a visual bug.

First playthrough: collect 2 wood -> click the wood nothing happens. Deleted the save, just in case. Second attempt: got to the part of rescuing on of the tiny dudes. It tells me to collect a flower but there are none on the map and you can't go past the "tutorial barrier". Really wanted to play the game 'cause it looked cozy, but I've already spent 2 hours on just trying for the tutorial to work and let me play. As a bonus, found one last bug before leaving: talk to any villager that creates a conversation bubble, press ESC, now you're stuck with that forever, nothing you do will dismiss the text. At this point I feel scammed :/

It is a small relaxing game, slightly buggy but you can easily finish it in a day or 2. I don't think there is much replayability because by the end of the first playthrough, you would have explored most of the biomes, characters and items. Bug 1 : Some achievements didn't pop, small issue but could trigger completionists. Bug 2 : After progressing quite deep into the game, somehow a certain resource did not spawn at all. I spent 10-15 minutes walking around but couldn't find it, got confused, check online and seems like there is a chance of such a thing occuring. The only way is to reset current progress and regenerate the map. I wanted to stop there and then because that means I have no idea if the bug will reoccur and reset my progress again. Decided to continue and the resource spawned properly, never encountering the issue again. As for the penalty from dying, I didn't die once because of all the other reviews making me super vigilant about it. I ended up reaching the max amount of steps by halfway through the game. I wish there is a QOL to tell you that you can't upgrade some attributes anymore but the option remains because you lose some if you die. If you grind a bit in the beginning, then you just snowball into having so much resources, the challenge later is to choose which item to drop. As what another reviewer highlighted, you can keep items on the ground only for the current quest, once you are ready to progress, remember to pick them all up. Overall, the game is too light to have any impact, if that is considered a downside. I don't feel like I played much of a game, even though it was okay while I was playing it.

Chill, cozy game. Took me 17 hours to beat. The graphics are pleasant. The gameplay is essentially point and click, with collecting, crafting, and trading. A great game for playing while listening to other music.

A great exploration rogue-lite game. Into the Emberlands lets you play as the Lightbearer & explore biomes, rescue Knacks, gather resources & rebuild your village while avoiding the mysterious Miasma.

Into the Emberlands is a cozy exploration game with a rogue-lite twist. As the Lightbearer, explore procedurally generated biomes, rescue lost Knacks and rebuild your village threatened by the Miasma.
In this cozy game you play as a Lightbearer, who must venture outside of the safety of your town to save lost villagers and collect resources.
'Into The Emberlands' has: 1 foil badge, 5 badges, 6 cards, 4 backgrounds, and 5 emoticons.
